question: After the 1857 Revolt, also known as India's first war of independence, Bahadur Shah Jafar, the last Mughal Emperor of India, was exiled to:
solution:
The correct answer is **Burma**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bahadur Shah Jafar** was the last Mughal Emperor of India.
 
• He was a symbolic leader during the **1857 Revolt**, which is also known as India's first war of independence.
 
• After the failure of the revolt, he was captured by the British forces.
 
• In 1858, he was exiled to **Burma** (present-day Myanmar), where he lived the remainder of his life.
 
• He died in exile in **Rangoon** (now Yangon) in 1862.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **1857 Revolt**: Also known as the Sepoy Mutiny, it was a major, but ultimately unsuccessful, uprising in India against the British East India Company's rule.
 
• **Bahadur Shah Zafar**: He was more of a symbolic figurehead during the revolt, as the actual fighting was led by Indian soldiers (sepoys) and local leaders.
 
• **British Repression**: The British brutally suppressed the revolt, leading to significant changes in their approach to ruling India.
 
• **End of Mughal Rule**: The exile of Bahadur Shah Zafar marked the official end of the Mughal Empire in India.
